description: Typed negative knowledge for the current ZenoDEX world-model baseline: falsifiers, blocked promotions, scope boundaries, implementation accidents, missing guards, and disputed assurance surfaces.

records.claim: Allocations that undershoot target_out can still be treated as exact-out winners.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: The world-model scenario shows that partial allocations stop denoting exact-out satisfaction, so canonical minimization over them is semantically invalid.
preconditions: target_out > 0
leg budget remains within the admitted search profile
records.replacement_claim: Exact-out winner selection only ranges over allocations that satisfy allocation_complete.
records.trigger: The allow_partial_exact_out_allocation scenario destroys exact-out semantics and leaves winner comparison underspecified.

records.claim: Stable runtime enumeration order is enough to justify exact-out canonicality.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: The previous symmetric counterexample has been repaired by switching the two-pool exact-out runtime tie-break to the explicit route_key_out. The remaining lesson still stands: runtime determinism is useful, but canonicality comes from the explicit total key plus candidate completeness, not from stable enumeration folklore.
preconditions: feasible exact-out allocations exist
one implementation happens to enumerate plateau candidates stably
records.replacement_claim: Canonicality comes from minimizing route_key_out = (input_total, leg_count, legs_lex) over complete candidates; the repaired two-pool runtime now reflects that key on the bounded emitted candidate set.
records.remaining_excluded_domain: Candidate domains outside the repaired bounded emitted set remain excluded: stable runtime enumeration is still not a semantic canonicality argument without explicit total-key minimization plus candidate completeness.
records.trigger: Dropping leg_count and legs_lex leaves equal-input winners semantically ambiguous even if one implementation returns the leftmost minimizer.

records.claim: The current bounded exact-out generator proves global optimality over all feasible allocations.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: The world model now records a Lean proof for finite-interval exact-out brute-force completeness, replayable many-pool emitted-domain quote minimality and certified-packet quote binding over audited emitted candidates, and a selected-domain CPMM projection-cover surface whose remaining local gap is only concrete emitted-path coverage on bounded audited domains. The remaining open work is now isolated as a generator soundness/completeness frontier rather than a canonicality frontier.
preconditions: candidate search is bounded by max_legs and the active search profile
the world model only reasons over emitted candidates
records.replacement_claim: Current support covers canonical minimization, finite-interval completeness over the emitted split search set, replayable emitted-domain quote minimality over audited many-pool candidates, a bounded selected-domain projection-cover certificate lane, and a replayable bounded workaround packet that compares the current runtime against the repaired broader bounded advisory surface; global generator completeness remains open.
records.trigger: The exact_out_canonical_minimizer slice now proves finite-interval completeness for the emitted split search set, but it still does not prove completeness across the full allocation space.

records.claim: Repairing the many-pool exact-out runtime over the selected bounded domain is enough to treat the full many-pool runtime as globally canonical.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: The previous bounded-domain runtime mismatch is repaired: on the old witness pools={(40,20),(40,63),(40,20)}, amount_out_total=3, the functional core now returns the canonical winner pool_b:3 with total input 2, matching the bounded certificate lane. There is now also a selected-domain support theorem, a selected-domain certified bridge theorem, a bounded projection-cover certificate carried by the route certificate on selected audited domains for the currently supported exact-out curve families, and a bounded advisory packet that consumes the repaired-bounded workaround by policy in the integration/API layer. The surviving negative knowledge is narrower: selected-domain canonicality still does not prove that the heuristic candidate-pool prefilter or the overall many-pool generator is globally complete.
preconditions: amount_out_total stays within the bounded audit budget
the audit enumerates the runtime-selected candidate-pool domain
route_key_out = (input_total, leg_count, legs_lex)
records.replacement_claim: The many-pool exact-out runtime is now canonically aligned over its selected bounded domain, and the integration/API layer exposes a default many-pool quote surface that advertises and matches replayable default packet build/verify aliases using the unified certified-advisory policy while lifting selected-domain and repaired-side projection-cover summaries to the top level, so the proof-backed selected-domain certified packet and repaired bounded advisory behavior are consumed together when they differ; the remaining open frontier is candidate-pool prefilter and generator completeness beyond that selected domain.
records.trigger: The functional core now delegates selected-domain winner selection to a bounded exact canonical-domain kernel, which repairs the old audited-domain counterexample, but the candidate-pool prefilter is still heuristic and the global generator-completeness frontier remains open.

records.claim: The current many-pool exact-out runtime prefilter is support-sound for bounded audited domains: every feasible bounded allocation uses only pools selected by the prefilter.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: Bounded witness: four identical pools `(40,20)` with `amount_out_total=2`. The prefilter selects `p0,p1,p2`, but the full bounded feasible domain still contains valid allocations using omitted pool `p3`; the canonical bad support witness is the one-leg quote `(p3:2)` with total input `5`. So the runtime prefilter does not satisfy the explicit support-soundness hypothesis even on this small audited domain.
preconditions: amount_out_total stays within the bounded audit budget
feasible pools are taken from the active exact-out direction
max_legs = 3
max_candidate_pools = 3
records.replacement_claim: The current runtime prefilter is not support-sound in general. The next honest frontier is either prefilter redesign or a stronger audited-domain condition, then generator completeness over the repaired boundary.
records.trigger: A bounded kernel audit enumerated the full feasible domain over all feasible pools and found a feasible allocation whose positive-leg support lies outside the selected prefilter set.

records.claim: The current settlement validator already gives one end-to-end certificate for every semantic lane.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: The repo now has one replayable end-to-end settlement certificate object for the settlement-certificate posture. validate_operations routes require_settlement_certificate through that packet, the packet nests a replayable feature-extension packet instead of trusting raw buyback/rebate/lock booleans, and Lean plus ESSO pin the deterministic rebuild and packet_ok shell for both the feature-extension packet and the end-to-end packet. The remaining limits are narrower: proof_ok and binding_ok are only locally derived when proof verification is enabled, and broader oracle-governance and endogenous-LP claims still live outside this packet shell.
preconditions: proof_flags are bound to a settlement witness
component proof lanes exist for cpmm, balance, token, proof, and binding checks
records.replacement_claim: Within settlement-certificate posture, the repo now uses one replayable end-to-end settlement certificate as the live acceptance object, with nested feature-extension and value lanes. The remaining frontier is deeper proof/internalization of proof-verification and oracle/LP semantics, not absence of a single certificate object.
records.trigger: The settlement-certificate runtime posture now routes through the unified settlement end-to-end certificate packet, the packet internalizes the feature-extension booleans through a nested replayable feature-extension packet, and Lean plus ESSO now pin the packetized acceptance shell.

records.claim: The compact settlement bundle is equivalent to the full two-step price rails surface.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: The compact settlement bundle only requires monotonicity plus |price_curr - price_prev| < 50, while the full price-rails contract also bounds the earlier |price_prev - price_pp| step. The repo now has both a Lean witness and a bounded Tau witness for that asymmetry.
preconditions: canonical replay ids are supplied to the settlement compact bundle
all component proof flags on the compact certificate are asserted true
records.replacement_claim: Full two-step price rails refine the compact settlement bundle surface, but the compact bundle remains a deliberately weaker certificate surface.
records.trigger: Lean and Tau evidence now exhibit the witness a=1, b=2, c=3, d=4, price_pp=0, price_prev=60, price_curr=70, where the compact bundle accepts but full two-step price rails reject.

records.claim: The new settlement spot-price packet already cryptographically authenticates the upstream price source.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: The packet remains a deterministic provenance surface: it binds price entries, source ids, freshness, and optional verified sync metadata, and ESSO cross-verifies that bounded gate. A separate optional BLS-signed attestation envelope now authenticates one normalized packet against a signer/source policy and a consumer-time age bound, but the packet itself still does not perform signature verification or certificate-path validation.
preconditions: a two-asset spot-price packet is built with positive prices and bounded freshness
any required cross-module sync contract verifies and remains green
records.replacement_claim: The settlement spot-price packet internalizes positivity, freshness, and optional sync semantics in a fail-closed packet, and an optional signed attestation can authenticate that packet against an allowlisted signer/source policy, but packet normalization alone is not cryptographic source authenticity.
records.trigger: The packet itself still only verifies deterministic normalization, freshness, and optional sync gating. There is now a separate signed attestation envelope for packet authenticity, but the packet alone is still not a cryptographic attestation.

records.claim: The LP-aware settlement value contract already proves endogenous LP valuation for settlement safety.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: The LP-aware contract makes LP rows explicit and mechanically checks that user LP value plus protocol LP liability cancels under the same unit value, and ESSO verifies that bounded law. A new endogenous LP settlement value packet now derives a reserve-marked LP unit value from pool reserves, LP supply, and attested or verified spot prices, but that still is not a full endogenous liquidation or unwind theorem.
preconditions: settlement carries lp_deltas
explicit asset prices are supplied through the raw map, price packet, or signed attestation path
explicit LP unit values are supplied for every pool referenced by lp_deltas
records.replacement_claim: The LP-aware settlement value contract now exposes LP rows and proves zero net value under declared asset prices and LP unit values when asset conservation and LP-liability balance hold, and the new endogenous LP settlement value packet packages a reserve-and-supply-derived LP reference value into one replayable contract object, but full endogenous LP pricing remains outside the proved settlement slice.
records.trigger: The LP-aware value sidecar proves internal LP user/liability cancellation only under the same declared LP unit values; it does not derive those unit values from pool state, market structure, or an endogenous oracle policy.

records.claim: ABI-compatible wrappers remain system-safe even if reserve and stake mirror synchronization is only a convention.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: The world model only treats composition as admissible when reserve and stake mirror invariants remain explicit and replayable.
preconditions: wrapper kernels preserve the public observables ABI
the composed system shares reserve or stake state across modules
records.replacement_claim: Wrapper equivalence is insufficient without explicit mirror-sync guards and system-spec replay.
records.trigger: Removing reserve_mirror_consistency or stake_mirror_consistency allows stale shared state to satisfy wrapper-local expectations while violating system safety.

records.claim: The public funding story is fully captured by funding_rate_market_v1 alone.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: Funding freshness, bounded-move gates, and witness conservation only compose cleanly when the witness lane remains part of the assurance surface.
preconditions: public assurance docs are treated as the source surface
epoch funding authorization is expected to compose with settlement semantics
records.replacement_claim: Perps funding admissibility requires the fresh-oracle gate and the decomposed witness settlement lane, not the market kernel in isolation.
records.trigger: The world model treats funding_rate_market_v1 plus funding_rate_settlement_witness_v1_1 as the decomposed public story, and settlement authorization remains sensitive to the witness lane.

records.claim: zUSD dual conservation is already promoted end to end into the executable assurance surface.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: The proof lane is stronger than the runtime assurance surface, so promotion is blocked until executable guards or certificates consume both conservation laws.
preconditions: debt and collateral homomorphism proofs compile
runtime transitions still need explicit conservation-facing acceptance gates
records.replacement_claim: The current posture proves dual conservation mathematically but has not yet promoted both laws into the executable assurance surface.
records.trigger: The world model records that removing collateral conservation weakens admissibility beneath the proof surface the slice describes.

records.claim: Local zUSD oracle validity is enough even when the composed perps oracle view materially diverges or lags.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: The repo now has both an explicit cross-module oracle sync contract packet and a fail-closed Tau replay surface that reject activation when divergence or epoch lag exceed configured bounds, which falsifies the stronger claim that module-local oracle validity alone is enough for composed safety.
preconditions: cross-module oracle composition is relevant to the deployment
the perps oracle snapshot is available for the synchronized market
records.replacement_claim: When deployments depend on a shared oracle world across zUSD and perps, oracle activation should be bound to the explicit divergence-and-lag sync contract; current support is contract-level and fail closed, but still opt-in and not yet kernel-backed.
records.trigger: The repo now exposes a deterministic divergence-and-lag sync gate for zUSD oracle activation against the perps oracle view, so local oracle validity alone is no longer the strongest composed shape.

records.claim: Review-packet coverage alone is enough to claim semantic replay parity for all runtime-active Tau specs.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: The new parity contract packet makes the distinction explicit: review-packet level passes across the whole active inventory, while semantic-contract level still records a bounded failing-spec set and inventory digest. That directly falsifies the idea that review coverage and semantic replay parity are interchangeable assurance surfaces.
preconditions: the active Tau inventory is generated from the current review manifest
the repo is making a semantic replay-parity claim rather than only a review-coverage claim
records.replacement_claim: Review-packet coverage is complete for active Tau specs, and the repo now has a dedicated parity contract that records the stronger semantic-contract posture and its current gaps without overclaiming equivalence.
records.trigger: The active inventory passes at review-packet level but still fails at semantic-contract level, so review coverage is not the same assurance surface as semantic replay parity.

records.claim: A verified signed spot-price attestation is already a complete oracle trust policy for settlement value safety.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: The new signed envelope improves the settlement boundary materially: it authenticates one canonical packet, enforces packet.now == signed_at, checks consumer-time freshness, and binds packet source ids to an allowlisted signer policy. That is still narrower than a complete oracle trust policy, because signer governance, source quorum, and disagreement policy remain external.
preconditions: a settlement spot-price packet is provenance-admissible
a BLS signer authenticates the packet and the signer/source allowlist accepts the packet source ids
consumer_now_epoch stays within the declared attestation age bound
records.replacement_claim: An optional signed spot-price attestation now gives packet authenticity plus signer/source-policy and age-bound enforcement at the normalized packet boundary, but complete oracle trust policy remains an external system concern.
records.trigger: The signed envelope authenticates one normalized packet against one local signer/source policy and one bounded age window, but it does not by itself internalize signer governance, key rotation, multi-source quorum, or broader oracle trust policy.

records.claim: The current many-pool exact-out runtime prefilter safely contracts bounded audited domains: every full bounded feasible candidate is key-dominated by some selected-domain candidate under route_key_out.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: Bounded witness: pools `(20,10)`, `(20,10)`, `(30,15)`, `(30,15)` with `amount_out_total=4`. The prefilter selects `p0,p2,p3`, but the full bounded canonical winner is `(p0:2,p1:2)` with total input `10`, and no selected-domain candidate has route_key_out less than or equal to that winner. So the runtime prefilter does not satisfy even the weaker safe-contraction condition on this small audited domain.
preconditions: amount_out_total stays within the bounded audit budget
feasible pools are taken from the active exact-out direction
max_legs = 3
max_candidate_pools = 3
records.replacement_claim: The current runtime prefilter is not safely contracting in general. A bounded cover-search selector already finds a repaired subset within the same candidate budget on the mixed-pool falsifier (`p0,p1`), and the generalized contraction audit confirms that repaired subset satisfies safe contraction on that witness. That repair principle is now packaged as a dedicated repaired-prefilter kernel, a replayable repaired-prefilter contract surface, and a replayable repaired advisory-quote packet surface with Lean- and ESSO-backed shell checks. On the deterministic 64-case bounded corpus over ordered four-pool products of `(20,10)` and `(30,15)` with `amount_out_total` in `{1,2,3,4}`, the current runtime prefilter matches the full bounded canonical winner in `61/64` cases, while the bounded repair matches in `64/64`, is never worse, and satisfies contraction in `64/64` cases. On the broader deterministic 405-case corpus over ordered four-pool products of `(20,10)`, `(30,15)`, and `(40,20)` with `amount_out_total` in `{1,2,3,4,5}`, the current runtime prefilter matches the full bounded canonical winner in `393/405` cases, while the repaired-prefilter kernel matches in `405/405`, is never worse, and satisfies contraction in `405/405` cases. The next honest frontier is to redesign the runtime prefilter around this repaired kernel or add a stronger audited-domain condition before attempting a global or bounded completeness bridge.
records.trigger: A bounded kernel audit enumerated both the full feasible domain over all feasible pools and the selected-domain candidate set, then found a full-domain candidate not dominated by any selected-domain candidate under route_key_out.

records.claim: For a fixed exact-in Pokayoke context, advisory action severity is monotone nondecreasing in amount_in.
records.evidence_or_falsifier: Concrete witness: amount_in=20 yields typed_confirm with high_price_impact, amount_in=21 yields confirm with moderate_price_impact, and amount_in=23 yields typed_confirm with mev_conflict plus high_price_impact.
preconditions: reserve_in = reserve_out = 500
fee_bps = 0
pending_volume_same_direction = 0
confidence_bps = 9000
user_slippage_bps = 10
slippage_options_bps = [10, 50, 100, 300, 500]
records.replacement_claim: The full advisory action surface is not monotone in amount_in. The honest runtime posture is a bounded deterministic probe schedule plus explicit regression witnesses until a smaller monotone subdomain is isolated and proved.
records.trigger: A bounded brute-force scan over adjacent amount_in values found a severity drop and later rebound in the same fixed pool/adversary context.
